name: Chicken Alfredo Lasagna

ingredients.item: Frozen Lightly Breaded Chicken Breast Bites
ingredients.buy: 2 lb 5 oz, baked from frozen and roughly chopped
a generous pinch of each (about 1 1/2 tsp salt and 3/4 tsp black pepper)

writer_notes: PROTEIN FLAG: source and locked protein is 'frozen lightly breaded chicken breast bites', a breaded convenience product, not plain boneless skinless chicken breast named in the run condition. Left locked; flagged for auditor ruling.
Ingredient-vs-step verified both directions: all 8 locked buy lines are used by a step, and no step uses anything unbought.
Salt buy line also carries pepper (about 1 1/2 tsp salt, 3/4 tsp black pepper); both go into the blend step, so prose says 'salt and pepper'.
21 no-boil sheets and 2 lb 5 oz chicken for 14 servings imply a 13x9 dish or two dishes; source used a 10.5x7.5 dish for the smaller un-scaled version. make_it states this.
Macros pass the enforced band: 496 cal (450-800), 40.7g protein (>=40), 34.4g carbs (unrestricted); noodles are the real carb source.
No cost_lines were provided in this dispatch, so shop_smart makes no per-ounce or per-package count claims; only the buy quantities from the locked view are referenced.
All macro references in prose use {{cal}}/{{protein}} tokens and cost uses ${{cost_ps}}; no literal numbers were computed.

prose.intro_html:
Chicken alfredo lasagna reads like a night out, the kind of plate you order and then quietly regret when the check lands. We are going to build it in your own kitchen instead, portion it across fourteen containers, and let the numbers do the talking. Each serving comes in at {{cal}} calories with {{protein}} grams of protein, which is a lot of creamy, cheesy comfort for a dinner you cook once and get to eat all week.

The quiet trick here is cottage cheese blended smooth right into the alfredo. It melts into the sauce, carries most of the protein, and keeps this from turning into the heavy kind of lasagna that puts you on the couch for the afternoon. Nobody at the table has to know it is in there, and your numbers will not either.
prose.shop_smart:
The chicken is the star of the list and the easiest place to shop smart. You want 2 lb 5 oz of frozen lightly breaded chicken breast bites, and the freezer aisle is exactly right here because you are baking it straight from frozen and chopping it after. No thawing, no trimming, nothing wasted.

For the cheese, grab 1 lb 2 1/2 oz of fresh mozzarella and shred it yourself with a few quick passes; roughly shredded is precisely what the layers want. The parmesan is 2 1/3 cups freshly grated, and grating a wedge yourself browns better on top than the shaker kind. Cottage cheese runs 4 2/3 cups, so plan your tubs to cover that, and round the cart out with 1 3/4 cups of alfredo sauce, 21 no-boil lasagna sheets, and a bunch of fresh parsley for the 6 tablespoons you will chop. That is the whole list, and none of it is fussy.
prose.make_it:
Heat the oven to 425 degrees. Bake or air fry the frozen chicken bites according to the bag, then roughly chop them into bite-size pieces once they are cooked through. That is the only real cooking before assembly, so get it done first.

Now the sauce. Blend the cottage cheese, the alfredo, and a generous pinch of salt and pepper until it is completely smooth. That blend is what makes this lasagna sit light instead of heavy, so do not shortcut it.

To build it, spread a thin layer of the blended sauce across the bottom of a large baking dish. A 13x9 works well, and for a batch this size you may want two dishes. Lay down 3 lasagna sheets, then more sauce, chopped chicken, parsley, mozzarella, and parmesan. Repeat the layers, but only use parsley on the first two so the top does not go bitter, and finish the very top with just mozzarella and parmesan.

Cover the dish and bake for 30 minutes. Uncover and bake another 10 to 15 minutes, until the cheese is bubbly and browning around the edges. Garnish with a little more fresh parsley and grated parmesan, then let it rest at least 5 minutes before you slice. That rest lets the layers set up so they portion clean instead of sliding apart.
prose.portion_html:
Here is how we land fourteen honest servings instead of eyeballing squares. Once the lasagna has rested, set an empty container on the scale and zero it out, then weigh the full pan of lasagna. Take that total weight, divide it by 14, and that is your target grams per container. Portion by weight, not by cutting even-looking squares, because the corners and the center are never the same and the scale does not play favorites.

Slice, lift, and load each of the fourteen containers to that number. Do it this way and every container carries the same {{cal}} calories and {{protein}} grams of protein, which is the entire point of prepping instead of guessing your way through the week.
prose.cost_closing_html: Cooked once and split fourteen ways, this comes out to ${{cost_ps}} per serving. That is a genuine chicken alfredo lasagna, three cheeses and breaded chicken and all, for less than you would leave as a tip on the same plate at a restaurant. Run that math across a week of dinners and the savings stop being pocket change and start being a line in your budget.

Membership runs a dollar a month, and it pays for itself the first time you swap one takeout night for a pan of this.

steps: Heat the oven to 425 degrees Fahrenheit.
Bake or air fry the frozen breaded chicken bites according to the package directions, then roughly chop into bite-size pieces once cooked through.
Blend the cottage cheese, alfredo sauce, and a generous pinch of salt and pepper until completely smooth.

Spread a thin layer of the blended sauce over the bottom of a large baking dish, then layer 3 lasagna sheets, more sauce, chopped chicken, parsley, mozzarella, and parmesan; repeat the layers, using parsley only on the first two, and finish the top with just mozzarella and parmesan.
Cover and bake for 30 minutes, then uncover and bake another 10 to 15 minutes until the cheese is bubbly and browning at the edges.
Garnish with fresh parsley and grated parmesan, rest at least 5 minutes, then slice and portion by weight into 14 containers.
